x: Wolton was second in the 880 and Hazel second in the mile. Sexton and Marshall running for their school, again completed a double for the first two places in the 100 and 220 yards and the school also won both the relay races.
A few junior events were also on the programme and Wolton was third in the 880 yards. Final scores were: H.H.H., 52 points; V.P.H., 48 points; Bels., 34 points.

In the 100 yards Tebbutt was second in his 10.8 secs. heat but failed in a 10.5 second round. Wolton failed to survive his 880 yards heat. In the 440 yards Morrison was second in a 54.3 heat but failed to get placed in a 51.8 final.

Placings of our team were: 1, Tooby, 21.17; 2, Stearman, 21.25; 4, Godfrey, 22.12; 5, Wolton, 22.49; 6, Briggs, 22.49; 8, Chitty, 23.48; 9, Butt, 23.51; 13, Burg, 24.50; 14, J.
Wolton third. Placings of our club members were as under:—Maclean, 1; Adams, P., 2; Wolton, 3; Simpson, 5; Greene, 6; Courtney, 7; Grieves, 8; Butt, 9; Udall, 11.
Mike Stearman was present to defend his 880 yards Junior title, but he was beaten by a newcomer to our ranks in Gerry Trower, with Bob Wolton third.

The senior 440 saw Ian Badiali gain a second title in quite fast time, and Jim Heathfield was a good second with Bob Wolton a plucky third. Don Maclean won the junior mile, as expected, and from the way he went off he seemed quite determined to make sure that Geoff Goode had no reserves of speed left.

We also had two races in the 440 yards Senior, and Bob Wolton won the first race, with "Jock" Cameron taking the second race. Wolton beat both Bob Taylor and Ian Badiali and is showing great improvement this season.

The 4 x 440 yds. saw Badiali, Wolton, Taylor and Cameron all run well to finish 3rd in their heat and so qualify for the final. In this we were again 3rd to Poly. and Woodford Green, and our time of 3 mins. 25.6 secs. would have won this event in previous years.
